story.head: Kucherov’s favorite opponent
paras: The Lightning won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-2 in Tampa Bay on Oct 8. The Lightning (8-3-2) lost 5-4 in a shootout to Nashville on Oct 31, while the Wild (10-3-3) beat Washington 5-1 on Sunday. Two of the league’s best teams meet. The Wild played last night, and the Lightning are rested. Going in, the Bolts are fourth in the Atlantic (tied for eighth in the NHL) and the Wild first in the Central (second).

The Lightning ice the puck less than almost anyone (3rd), get into a lot of chippy games (3rd) and let the point shots come and guard the net (4th). On the other side, the Wild draw more penalties than they take (2nd), but get pinned in their own end on long shifts (31st). They also leave the shooting to their forwards (3rd lowest), so the Lightning’s defensemen shoot a lot, and theirs not so much. Minnesota has allowed 2.25 goals a game, the third fewest in the league. Something has to give when the Wild’s shooting runs into the Lightning’s defense.

Nikita Kucherov (4 G / 14 A / 18 P in 13 GP) leads the Lightning in scoring, with eight points in his last five games and a point in seven straight games against Minnesota. Brandon Hagel (8 G / 8 A / 16 P in 13 GP) has a team-high eight goals. Kirill Kaprizov (15 G / 10 A / 25 P in 16 GP) leads the Wild in scoring and is third in the NHL, with eight points in his last five games and five goals in six games against Tampa Bay since 2023-24. Quinn Hughes (5 G / 16 A / 21 P in 16 GP) isn’t far behind, with eight points in his last five games.

Andrei Vasilevskiy (6-3-1 / .877 SV% in 10 GS) will likely start for Tampa Bay, and Calvin Pickard (1-1-0 / .833 SV% in 2 GS) for Minnesota. Vasilevskiy has a .877 save percentage in six starts against the Wild, well under his usual .910. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
